scope: Reviewed the supported font-program behavior against the local Adobe Type 1 Font Format (chapters 2, 3, 5-8 and 10), TN 5176 CFF (sections 2-19, appendices A-C/F/H), TN 5177 Type 2 (sections 2-4, appendices A-C), and TN 5014 CIDFont (sections 2.3/2.4, 3.2 and 4.1/4.2). The itemized verdicts below distinguish corrected behavior, agreement, unhinted outline policy and incomplete structural validation; this is not full PostScript or font conformance certification. The previous PDF-side review remains ISO 32000-2:2020 sponsored EC3, 9.6.3, 9.6.5.1/2/4, 9.7.4.1/2/3, 9.9.1/2 and Tables 124/125. Remaining primary-format review includes: OpenType/ISO 14496-22 and TrueType Reference Manual (including CFF2), TN 5015 Type 1 supplements including lenIV -1, and TN 5040 PFB packaging. Project budgets are separate from format limits. Reported recovery is checked as ADR 0003 project policy against ISO 9.9.1/Table 124 and PDF cmap selection in 9.6.5.4; unknown charstring escape policy is checked against Type 1 6.3/Appendix 2 and TN 5177 3.3/Appendix A. The sfnt alignment, extent, loca, component-flag and cmap layout details still await full TrueType/OpenType primary-format review; corpus inspection is secondary evidence, not primary-format verification. Static Type 1 RD/ND/NP aliases and bounded procedure definitions have additionally been checked against Type 1 2.4, 7.3 and 10.3. CFF blue-hint ordering recovery is checked against TN 5176 section 15/Table 23 and Type 1 5.3-5.5: each zone pair ascends, while zones themselves need not be globally sorted. FontProgram retained_bytes is an ADR 0012 accounting model, not a format requirement or allocator measurement. DICT recovery was additionally reviewed against TN 5176 section 4/Table 6, section 15/Table 23 and Appendix H; encoding supplement recovery against section 12/Tables 14-15; repeated Type 1 CharStrings names against chapters 6 and 10. First-definition retention and dropping malformed metadata are explicit ADR 0003 choices, not claims that the format standards prescribe those recoveries. Descriptor flag-pair validity and the reader's selection routes were checked against local ISO 32000-2:2020 sponsored EC3 9.8.2/Table 121, 9.6.5.1/Table 112, 9.6.5.2, 9.6.5.4 and Annex D.2/Table D.2. The review distinguishes invalid pairs from informational repertoire disagreement: valid flags retain the prescribed selection algorithm, including its permitted reader fallbacks. No repertoire heuristic overrides a valid pair; only invalid pairs require this reported repair. Program glyph-name lookup and extraction-only Unicode fallback were additionally checked against local ISO 32000-2:2020 sponsored EC3 9.10.2: ToUnicode and encoding/collection mappings retain priority, followed by an explicit reader choice to apply the existing AGL converter to the selected glyph name. This does not alter painting or claim new primary verification of TrueType post layouts. Glyph-name list scoping was checked against ISO 9.10.2 and Annex D.6/Table D.6 and the local Adobe Glyph List: numeric ZapfDingbats names are not general AGL names. Family aliases and recognized subset/style spellings are explicit reader policy.

cmap8_review.rule: Format 8 has a long header, 8192-byte word-length bitmap and sorted, disjoint sequential groups. Glyph ranges must fit maxp. The API receives one complete numeric code; it does not decode an encoded word stream.
cmap8_review.implementation: The existing group validator and binary lookup also handle format 8, retaining the original table bytes. It validates bitmap extent, ordering, glyph bounds and declared group budgets; no range is expanded. Format 8 permits numeric keys across u32 while formats 12/13 retain the Unicode ceiling. Existing subtable selection remains unchanged, preferring 12/10 before 8 before BMP formats.
cmap8_review.scope: Microsoft's UTF-16 introduction and UCS4 high-word example disagree; Apple also differs on bitmap bit order. This change does not adjudicate a stream decoder or validate bitmap encoding semantics. It looks up the caller's numeric key unchanged, preserving PDF glyph-name selection and all existing cmap identities.
cmap8_review.expectations: Native controls distinguish BMP, scalar and packed-surrogate numeric keys, gaps, group order/overlap, glyph overflow, exact work/entry bounds, truncated headers/groups and one deduplicated repair. Format 12/13 shared-path controls preserve sequential/constant mapping and their Unicode ceiling. Eight PDF controls retain the earlier diagnostic bytes and literal rectangle oracles; isolated supplementary cases map the literal PDF byte to a different glyph.

collection_review.rule: TTC headers 1/2 locate per-face sfnt directories; table offsets remain relative to the whole file and tables can be shared. Naming-table ID 6 supplies restricted ASCII PostScript names, encoded according to its platform. Versions 0/1 have bounded record and string-storage extents.
collection_review.implementation: One directory reader handles standalone and selected collection faces. The original FontBytes owner is retained without rewriting shared tables; other faces are scanned only for names when requested. Native callers select an index or ordered exact name hints. An ambiguous earliest match is rejected, even if a later hint is unique. PDF loading tries exact FontName/BaseFont, followed by those names without a valid six-letter subset tag. Standalone programs ignore collection name hints.
collection_review.scope: PDF Table 124 supplies no collection index; PDF named selection is measured reader policy, not a claimed normative embedding requirement. DSIG is inert and range checked, not authenticated. Checksums, hint execution, nondefault variations and unselected glyph validation remain outside this change.
collection_review.expectations: The 20 original diagnostic fixture records and all PDF/PPM bytes are unchanged. Ten native vectors cover indices/names, shared original storage, TTC versions 1/2, a selected directory after its shared tables, and an inert DSIG header. Unit controls cover name versions/encodings, ambiguity/priority, invalid or absent names, truncation and limits.
collection_review.evidence: Diagnostic 4aa3d18ce2c9c1f5d35353150eff29bab5188f80, hosted run40413575630: pdf.js passes all 22 controls, including both named faces in simple/CID TrueType and CID OpenType CFF. verification.external_status: TN 5176/5177 and applicable TN 5014 reviewed; current CFF2 Top/Font/Private DICT namespaces reviewed; other CFF2 primary review remains pending
verification.evidence: Secondary read-fonts 0.41.0 comparison: 668 glyph-name mappings and 1792 code mappings across the seven metadata fixtures agree, with undefined entries normalized against GID 0; the gap at ExpertEncoding code 92 was corrected following that comparison. Analytic fixtures exercise FDSelect 4 and Private DICT blends; no external known-answer dataset or primary-format verification. Secondary skrifa 0.46.2 agrees on bounds and curve counts of six default CFF2 glyphs: static, charstring blend, inherited/overridden Private DICT blends, FDSelect 4 and FD index 256. The historical Font DICT matrix disagreement led to an explicit refusal; current primary review below supersedes that refusal without rewriting its recorded observations. These secondary comparisons are not primary-text verification. Primary review now confirms the 391 standard strings, both full 256-code encodings and both Expert charset orders. Type 2 operators, limits and analytic expectations were checked against TN 5177; this supersedes the earlier pending status for those definitions.
verification.choices: Unhinted API retains flex curves, skips hint placement and ignores allowed embedded PostScript. Type 2 random uses a per-glyph 32-bit LCG seeded from folded initialRandomSeed bits, returning (state+1)/2^32; the texts specify seed and range but not the algorithm. Uninitialized transient reads use zero (undefined by TN 5177), invalid index ranges and nonfinite arithmetic fail, zero-element roll is a no-op. CFF2 default-instance interpretation retains its earlier secondary evidence and pending primary review. Unknown-operator handling follows the explicit stack rule with the same source's DICT-data wording conflict recorded below; legacy matrix application remains separate.

requirements.status: Bounded static Type 1 procedure bindings and assignments, including symbolic and explicitly declared custom names.
requirements.gaps: This remains a static extractor, not full PostScript validation. Computed readers or assignment procedures, nested procedure execution, arbitrary alias expansion and unrecognized executable forms use font.type1-postscript.

verification.primary_text: Local Adobe Type 1 Font Format; TN 5176 CFF
verification.rule: RD reads an exact length of binary charstring bytes; ND defines a dictionary entry; NP stores a subroutine array entry. Chapter 2 explicitly permits symbolic aliases and definitions outside the Private dictionary. Subroutine zero may hold an ordinary charstring when flex and hint replacement are unused (8.4).
verification.verdict: agrees with the documented scope; independent vectors and API invariants tested
verification.implementation: Recognize RD/-|, ND/|-, NP/| plus custom names bound to the exact static reader/def/put bodies. Match declarations and assignments without evaluating PostScript; bound token lengths, nesting, work and binding count. Canonical aliases remain available for the pre-existing abbreviated static extraction convention.
verification.expectations: Independent Python font writers derive paths and metrics analytically; Rust API tests check the documented memory model and stable recovery tags without importing or running the engine from the generator.

requirements.status: Reported recovery of unused blue-zone operator and pair ordering, across bare/CID/OpenType CFF and CFF2.
requirements.gaps: Complete validation of blue-zone cardinality, distances and BlueScale constraints is outside this unhinted API. CFF2 primary text remains unavailable; its matching unhinted recovery is a documented project choice.

verification.primary_text: Local Adobe Type 1 Font Format; TN 5176 CFF
verification.rule: OtherBlues follows BlueValues and FamilyOtherBlues follows FamilyBlues. Each individual lower/upper zone pair ascends; zone pairs need not be globally sorted. In delta encoding the second delta of each pair is nonnegative.
verification.verdict: agrees with the documented scope; independent vectors and API invariants tested
verification.implementation: Strict mode rejects font.cff-blue-order. Repair mode keeps original bytes and ignores only ordering of unused hint metadata; widths, subroutines and paths remain unchanged. No zones are sorted. The delta sign test avoids accumulating unused absolute coordinates. All diagnostics pass through the public parse sink.
verification.expectations: Independent Python font writers derive paths and metrics analytically; Rust API tests check the documented memory model and stable recovery tags without importing or running the engine from the generator.

repairs.rule: Ignore operator/pair ordering faults in unused blue hints, with strict rejection and reported repair.

requirements.status: A cached, saturating estimate of each parsed program's retained heap, independent of glyph use and clones.
requirements.gaps: Allocator padding/fragmentation and private core Name representation are estimated. A clone reports the full shared estimate; callers charge once per distinct program. pagura-text uses the estimate and charges its own outer Arc and FontProgram value separately.

verification.locator: ADR 0012 retained-cache accounting model; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md performance policy
verification.rule: Count original input and parsed-state Arc allocations, owned vector capacities and nested buffers, encodings, name/CID trees and variation data once. The estimate is not peak memory or allocator telemetry.
verification.verdict: agrees with the documented scope; independent vectors and API invariants tested
verification.implementation: Compute once at successful parse and return a cached usize. Input bytes and CFF INDEX ranges are not double-counted. Type 1 decrypted subroutines/charstrings are retained separately. Tree entries add 64 bytes of estimated bookkeeping and names add logical payload lengths, conservatively including inline names. Exclude FontProgram inline storage, a caller-owned surrounding Arc, temporary parsing/outlining and external diagnostics.
verification.expectations: Independent Python font writers derive paths and metrics analytically; Rust API tests check the documented memory model and stable recovery tags without importing or running the engine from the generator.

requirements.status: Reported recovery of unused hint operand arity and reserved operator slots; consumed values and dictionary domains remain strict.
requirements.gaps: No general DICT salvage or CFF2 operator recovery. Invalid numeric encodings, structural ambiguity, consumed values, duplicate known operators and resource limits remain errors.

verification.rule: DICT operators consume the preceding operand group, arrays and deltas have one or more values, and scalar hints have one value. Appendix H marks reserved operator slots. It does not define how to recover them.
verification.verdict: format rule reviewed; recovery is documented ADR 0003 policy, tested with independent vectors
verification.implementation: Discard only malformed unused Private hint entries. Skip reserved operator slots and clear their operands. Keep widths, offsets, matrices, seed operands and known operators in the wrong dictionary fatal. Reserved number markers 31 and 255 remain errors because no payload size is defined.
verification.expectations: The independent Python writer supplies chosen rectangles, widths, names and mappings. Strict tags and exact repaired results are checked together; rejected consumed operands and numeric markers are tested in repair mode as well.

repairs.rule: Skip reserved operator slots and discard only their preceding operands.

requirements.status: Reported first-definition retention for repeated CharStrings names, including .notdef and the empty name.
requirements.gaps: No PostScript execution or inference of computed bindings. Unreadable record lengths and nonstatic terminators remain fatal. Repeated empty names are not classified as invalid name syntax.

verification.rule: CharStrings binds character names to length-delimited encrypted procedures. The book describes dictionary bindings and does not require first-definition retention for repeated physical assignments.
verification.verdict: format rule reviewed; recovery is documented ADR 0003 policy, tested with independent vectors
verification.implementation: Strict mode rejects repeated names as an ambiguity of static extraction. Repair mode consumes each later binary record and checks its terminator, then drops it without allocating or decrypting a retained glyph. The first binding, widths and outlines stay intact; .notdef remains GID zero. This is explicit project policy, not execution of PostScript replacement semantics.
verification.expectations: The independent Python writer supplies chosen rectangles, widths, names and mappings. Strict tags and exact repaired results are checked together; rejected consumed operands and numeric markers are tested in repair mode as well.

repairs.rule: Keep the first static binding for each name.

requirements.status: Reported omission of invalid or incomplete supplemental mappings while retaining the main encoding and valid records.
requirements.gaps: Invalid main encodings and unusable charsets still reject. Dropped records provide no guessed mapping. Record truncation can only be detected within the available CFF buffer because the format has no encoding byte length.

verification.rule: A supplement gives another code to a glyph already named by the main encoding. Records contain a one-byte code and a SID, preceded by their count.
verification.verdict: format rule reviewed; recovery is documented ADR 0003 policy, tested with independent vectors
verification.implementation: Drop records whose SID is not main-encoded or whose code is already mapped. Keep the main mapping or first accepted supplementary mapping; retain later valid records. Drop an incomplete remaining tail without fabricating SIDs or codes. Original charstrings and widths are untouched.
verification.expectations: The independent Python writer supplies chosen rectangles, widths, names and mappings. Strict tags and exact repaired results are checked together; rejected consumed operands and numeric markers are tested in repair mode as well.

repairs.rule: Omit unusable supplemental records; never overwrite existing codes.

requirements.status: Only invalid Symbolic/Nonsymbolic pairs are repaired in the shared renderer loader; valid pairs retain the prescribed selection routes without repertoire diagnostics.
requirements.gaps: Direct pagura-text PdfFont::load calls retain strict pair validation; that API has no shared recovery hook. TrueType/OpenType binary layouts remain pending primary-text review. Character-set metadata is not exhaustively validated and does not override selection.

verification.rule: Exactly one of Symbolic and Nonsymbolic is set; Symbolic is the primary reader bit. For Type 1, PDF Encoding overrides built-in names irrespective of the flags. TrueType uses the given flags and Encoding for named cmap/post selection or raw byte selection, with reader-selected mappings allowed after the specified routes fail. A character-set disagreement alone does not require departing from this algorithm.
verification.verdict: Corrected: the previous repertoire heuristic reported valid flag pairs even when the prescribed algorithm could be followed. The implementation now preserves every valid pair and applies the existing 9.6.5 selection routes and permitted fallbacks. Invalid pairs alone need descriptor normalization.
verification.implementation: A temporary bounded descriptor view preserves Symbolic and makes Nonsymbolic its inverse only when both bits are set or both are clear. All other bits and source objects stay unchanged. Valid pairs are passed directly to the existing PDF font loader, without decoding a probe glyph, classifying the repertoire, changing routes or emitting this tag. Symbolic ignores Encoding references; missing Encoding also selects raw bytes. Named selection retains the mandated cmap/post priority before the permitted reader fallbacks. Invalid CID pairs are normalized without changing CID/CMap selection.
verification.expectations: Independent generated mappings, empty and rectangular glyphs, explicit PDF widths and Unicode pin raw versus named selection. Both/neither reject Strict with the descriptor tag and identity; Repair preserves Symbolic. Valid single flags, including Type 1 repertoire disagreement, Unicode-only Symbolic cmaps, symbol-only Nonsymbolic fallback, post names and ignored cyclic Encoding, succeed Strict without diagnostics. Exact pixels, glyph IDs, widths, extraction, preserved non-selection bits and immutable original dictionaries are checked.

repairs.rule: Only both-set or both-clear pairs are normalized; Symbolic remains primary and Nonsymbolic becomes its inverse. A valid pair is never reclassified from repertoire metadata. The prescribed routes and their permitted fallbacks do not trigger this tag.

requirements.status: Constant-time glyph-index name lookup for TrueType post, name-keyed Type 1 and CFF; shared program metadata is included in retained-byte estimates. Post 2.5 signed standard-name offsets reuse the same index and work/entry limits; post 1 requires all 258 standard glyphs. The post 2.5 and reserved-index changes passed hosted checks; post 4 admission passes all 17 integrated rendering controls at b1fd431a8, and its three-platform functional run 40393127365 passes.
requirements.gaps: Custom post name validation and Apple-only post 4 printer-name derivation remain open; post 4 numeric code arrays are admitted for existing cmap selection. CID-keyed CFF and bare CFF2 charsets do not provide glyph names. The primary review below covers post 1/2.5 count and index rules; it is not full OpenType certification.

verification.primary_text: Local ISO 32000-2:2020 sponsored EC3; Adobe Type 1 Font Format; Adobe TN 5176 CFF
verification.locator: PDF 9.10.2; Type 1 chapter 6; CFF section 13; ADR 0012
verification.rule: Type 1 and name-keyed CFF identify glyph programs by names. A reader may supply Unicode when the stated character-code mappings fail.
verification.verdict: Primary PDF/Type 1/CFF rules reviewed; use of program names after the specified mappings fail is an explicit reader choice. Selected post 1/2.5 binary rules are reviewed separately below.
verification.implementation: Names are indexed once by glyph ID, within decoded-byte budgets. Duplicate post names remain available on each glyph; name-to-glyph lookup retains its first match. Type 1 indexing follows normalization of .notdef to glyph zero. Missing names return None, including out-of-range IDs. The reverse index is accounted in FontProgram::retained_bytes and shared by clones. Index size, payload and glyph-range errors retain the source table/program offset rather than zero.
verification.expectations: Independent fonts provide repeated post names at distinct glyphs, standard post indices, a reordered Type 1 .notdef, CFF SIDs and nameless CID/CFF2 charsets. Both forward lookup and reverse identity are checked, with unchanged outline oracles.

post_review.rule: Post 1 implies exactly 258 glyphs. Post 2.5 uses tag 0x00025000, a count matching maxp, and one signed byte added to each glyph ID to index the standard-name set. Post 2 name indices 32768 through 65535 are reserved.
post_review.implementation: The existing names owner validates both index bounds and count equality, and sends borrowed standard names through its existing bounded index builder. No offset array, custom-name copy path or new parser is added.
post_review.expectations: Literal signed offsets cover .notdef, A, .null, B, space and the final standard name; all truncations, count mismatch, both index bounds, and exact work/entry boundaries are checked. The earlier five-glyph post-1 fixture was nonconforming; its named-glyph control now supplies 258 glyphs, with the undersized count retained as an explicit unit refusal. The final permitted custom index is accepted; reserved indices fail before custom-name allocation even under a zero-entry budget.
post_review.scope: Post 2.5 is deprecated but remains a defined legacy input. Other font-format obligations stay open. Legacy post4 composite-code arrays are admitted for unchanged cmap use after count/work validation; they do not supply name strings in this implementation. Printer-derived names remain unimplemented.

requirements.status: Positioned extraction uses the selected glyph name only after existing Unicode mappings fail. Painting and PdfFont::decode are unchanged.
requirements.gaps: Unnamed glyphs and names unknown to the existing AGL converter remain unknown. No Unicode is inferred from literal raw bytes, glyph indices, font names or inverse cmap guesses. Composite-font collection mappings retain priority.

verification.primary_text: Local ISO 32000-2:2020 sponsored EC3; local Adobe Glyph List data
verification.locator: 9.10.2 priority list and final paragraph; 9.6.5.2/4; Adobe Glyph List 2.0; Annex D.6/Table D.6
verification.rule: ToUnicode has first priority, followed by names used in selection or the applicable CID collection mapping. If these fail, a reader may choose another character mapping.
verification.verdict: Primary mapping order reviewed; program-name fallback is explicitly reader policy under the final paragraph, not a repair or a claim that raw selection used that name.
verification.implementation: Only the optional positioned-text recorder performs fallback. Existing Unicode, including an explicit empty string, is retained. Otherwise an outline glyph can supply a program name to the same AGL converter the text decoder already uses. No recovered text is passed back to glyph selection, metrics or painting. Name-processing work and retained output bytes are separately bounded. Composite collection mappings retain priority before program-name fallback. AGL and ZapfDingbats names are separate lists. The latter is used only for a recognized ZapfDingbats/Dingbats base font, including recognized subset/style names; other fonts and absent base names get AGL alone. This policy also applies to encoding-name conversion. ToUnicode remains authoritative.
verification.expectations: Independent pairs cover both-set and valid Symbolic flags with and without post names, AGL suffix/component and supplementary-scalar rules, authoritative ToUnicode, authoritative encoding names and unknown names. Exact pixels and glyph IDs remain fixed; decoded glyph text and positioned fallback text are checked separately. Independent a12/a19 vectors cover ordinary and Dingbats fonts on raw and named routes. Annex D.6 gives the hand and check-mark identities; those names are absent from the local AGL. All vectors retain exact rectangle pixels and metrics.

requirements.status: Selected OpenType vertical single substitutions for external CID provider fonts; PDF metrics and extraction stay independent. Synthetic maps, malformed-input/resource bounds, bundled CJK substitutions and PDF metrics/extraction controls pass the three-platform hosted functional checks at 6ac4b1d27 (run40385513689).

verification.primary_text: Microsoft OpenType 1.9.1 GSUB, OpenType Layout Common Table Formats, registered vert/vrt2 features; PDF 2.0 EC3 9.7.4.3 and 9.7.5.
verification.rule: Select the script and language feature indices, prefer vrt2 to vert, apply deduplicated lookups in LookupList order and the first matching subtable per lookup. Single substitutions change glyph identities, never PDF W/W2/DW/DW2 or ToUnicode.
verification.implementation: The existing sfnt owner lazily reads selected GSUB type 1 or type 7-to-1 lookups. FontProgram compiles a bounded immutable map, and PdfFont owns it only for external vertical CID substitutes.
verification.expectations: Original synthetic sfnt/GSUB bytes have literal glyph maps, an independent horizontal/vertical PDF metric and extraction pair, malformed tables, truncated selected tables and exact work/entry bounds. Existing bundled Adobe collection fixtures retain PDF bytes.
verification.choices: For Adobe collections, the provider policy requests hani with JAN/ZHS/ZHT/KOR by collection and falls back to DFLT/default LangSys when absent. This is a substitution policy, not general script shaping or an embedded CID/GID rewrite.
verification.outside: GDEF-dependent lookup filters, contextual/multiple/alternate/ligature substitutions, nonzero FeatureVariations, arbitrary shaping and unsupported provider/collection coverage. Other TrueType/OpenType primary-format review remains pending.
verification.verdict: Primary-defined selected layout subset implemented and validated by the scoped hosted controls at 6ac4b1d27. Competitive-family acceptance remains unprobed.
